---
name: start-worktree
description: >-
  OPT-IN tool for working on two things at once. Creates an isolated git worktree
  with its OWN dev env (its own Supabase + Next.js on unique ports) so a second
  effort can run without colliding with whatever already holds the main checkout —
  most commonly building something while an erlich loop is already running, or
  several agents/people working the same repo in parallel. Do NOT use this for
  ordinary single-track work: just work in the main checkout on a feature branch
  with `make dev`. Trigger when the user explicitly asks to "work on this in
  parallel", "spin up a worktree", "isolate this", "run two things at once", or when
  another effort (a loop, another agent) already occupies the main dev env. To
  VERIFY existing work use verify-changes; to build just one thing, stay in the main
  checkout.
---

# Start work in an isolated worktree (opt-in — for parallel work)

Reach for this **only when you need a second workspace running at the same time as
the first** — e.g. you want to keep building while an erlich loop is mid-run, or
several agents/people are working the same repo at once. A worktree gets its own
branch **and** its own dev env (own Supabase + Next.js on unique ports), so the two
tracks don't fight over ports, processes, or local data.

> **Default path — no worktree.** For ordinary single-track work, don't use this
> skill. Just work in the **main checkout** on a feature branch and run `make dev`:
> one env, one set of ports, simpler and faster. Branch → build → verify in the
> running app → PR. Only come here when a *second* concurrent track needs its own
> space.

> Announce at start: "Using start-worktree — since you want a second track running
> in parallel, I'll set it up in its own worktree on its own ports so it won't
> collide with the main dev env."

## Step 0 — read git state (it decides how to start)

Run `git fetch origin`, `git status`, `git branch --show-current` first, then:

| State | What it means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| **Clean tree on `main`** | fresh start | Pull (`git pull`), then create a worktree on a **new branch off `origin/main`**. |
| **Uncommitted changes on `main`** | the changes probably belong on a feature branch | **Confirm with the user** ("move these into the new worktree?"). On yes, MOVE them (stash → create worktree → pop). |
| **On a feature branch in the main checkout** | you're already mid-work here | That's fine — you can keep working right here in the main checkout. Only move this branch into its own worktree if you need the main checkout free for *another* track to run in parallel. |
| **Already inside a worktree** | you're set | Just bring its env up — `make worktree-env-up` (skip the rest). |

## Step 1 — name the branch

Ask for the task in plain product terms. Branch convention: `feat/<short-slug>`
(a short kebab-case description of the work).

## Step 2 — create the worktree (and move local changes in, if any)

Create it with the `EnterWorktree` tool, or fall back to `git worktree add`.
Worktrees live at `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`.

```bash
# from-scratch start (clean tree on main):
git worktree add -b feat/<slug> /abs/path/.claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main
```

**Moving uncommitted changes from main into the new worktree** (the confirmed
case) — stash includes untracked files, and the stash is repo-global so it pops
cleanly in the new tree:

```bash
# in the main checkout, after the user confirms:
git stash push -u -m "start-worktree: move to feat/<slug>"
git worktree add -b feat/<slug> /abs/path/.claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main
cd /abs/path/.claude/worktrees/<name>
git stash pop          # changes now live here, uncommitted
git status             # confirm: changes present here, main is clean
```

If `git stash pop` conflicts (main was behind and your edits touch files that
moved upstream), resolve in the worktree — that's the rebase-onto-latest you'd
have hit anyway.

## Step 3 — bring up the isolated env

From inside the new worktree:

```bash
make worktree-env-up      # deterministic unique ports; see worktree-dev
```

It allocates a free port block, patches `supabase/config.toml` (`project_id` +
ports), seeds/overrides env, runs `supabase start` + migrations, and starts the
Next.js app (web + `app/api/*` + `app/api/mcp`) on its shifted `:3000` port.
`make worktree-env-status` shows the block; you'll get the URLs on success.

> A freshly-started worktree DB has migrations applied but **no e2e seed**
> (`profiles` is empty). If your work needs a logged-in user or specific rows,
> seed them: hit `POST /api/auth/dev-session` (gated on `MOCK_CLIENTS`) to mint
> the `dev@vibes.test` user, then run the e2e seed helpers in
> `apps/next/e2e/` (`seed.ts`) or apply `supabase/seed.sql`.

## Step 4 — you're ready to work

Confirm the hand-off: working in worktree `<name>` on branch `feat/<slug>`, env
on its own ports; the main checkout is untouched and free to keep running the
other track. Build here. When the work is done, verify it (`verify-changes` if you
want the isolated deep check), open the PR, and after merge run
`make worktree-env-down` + remove the worktree to free the block.

## start-worktree vs verify-changes

- **start-worktree** (this) — *begin* a second, parallel piece of work in its own
  isolated workspace (and move your local changes into it).
- **verify-changes** — *review/verify* existing work. Its default is the dev env
  you're already running; the isolated-worktree side-by-side is its opt-in deep
  check.

## Quick reference

| Need | Go to |
|---|---|
| Create the worktree (native or git fallback) | `EnterWorktree` / `git worktree add` |
| Bring the isolated env up/down/status | `make worktree-env-up` / `worktree-dev` |
| Seed a logged-in dev user / test rows | `POST /api/auth/dev-session`, `apps/next/e2e/`, `e2e-testing` |
| Verify the work once it's built | `verify-changes` |
| Just building one thing? | Skip this — stay in the main checkout with `make dev` |

# from-scratch start (clean tree on main):
git worktree add -b feat/<slug> /abs/path/.claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main

# in the main checkout, after the user confirms:
git stash push -u -m "start-worktree: move to feat/<slug>"
git worktree add -b feat/<slug> /abs/path/.claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main
cd /abs/path/.claude/worktrees/<name>
git stash pop          # changes now live here, uncommitted
git status             # confirm: changes present here, main is clean
make worktree-env-up      # deterministic unique ports; see worktree-dev
